subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & subprocessors (PII, retention, residency)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Data handling & subprocessors (PII, retention, residency)

Hi Alice / Bob,

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and the next steps we discussed on data handling and third-party sharing:

Summary of what we covered:
- Types of PII you might surface via API calls (names, emails, small IDs) and our recommended prompt patterns to avoid unnecessary sensitive data being sent.
- Data retention options: live request-level logs (14 days default), optional longer retention for debugging (30/90/365 days) under contract.
- Logging controls: sampling, redaction hooks, and per-route log level configuration.
- Data residency: hosted US, EU regions; Dedicated/Private for strict residency and VPC options.
- Subprocessors: telemetry vendors (Sentry/Datadog), cloud infra providers (GCP, AWS), marketplace flows (Azure marketplace broker).

Requested next steps from Acme:
1) Alice: send the detailed security/compliance checklist questions you want prioritized.
2) Bob: procurement will want our Subprocessor List + DPA and SOC2 report — attaching initial artifacts.
3) Redwood (Logan/Dev): confirm whether telemetry payloads contain any user content by default and what redaction options exist.

Attachments included: redwood_subprocessors_list_20260322.pdf, SOC2_report_redwood_2025.pdf, data_processing_addendum_acme.docx

If helpful I can put together a short Mutual Action Plan — let me know timeline constraints.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com

From: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Bob Sullivan <bob.sullivan@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & subprocessors (PII, retention, residency)

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. A couple of clarifying questions from our security team after reviewing the attachments:

1) Telemetry vendors: you list Datadog and Sentry as telemetry subprocessors. Does outbound telemetry include any request/response bodies or only metadata (latency, errors, trace ids)? If bodies are included, can we disable that?

2) Cloud providers: where are logs stored by default for the hosted offering? Is there an option to keep logs strictly in the US region for Acme org?

3) Marketplace flows: we plan to procure via our Azure marketplace subscription — does that introduce any additional data sharing with Microsoft (invoice/billing metadata vs. request payloads)?

4) Data retention: you mentioned sampling/redaction hooks. Can you confirm whether Redwood supports automatic PII redaction for common patterns (emails, credit card numbers)? If not automated, what is the recommended approach?

Can you please respond to these points and flag anything that would require a redline in the DPA?

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Head of Security, Acme Corp
alice.chen@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme.com>, Bob Sullivan <bob.sullivan@acme.com>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 12:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data handling & subprocessors (PII, retention, residency)

Alice — good questions. Answering inline and adding next steps below.

1) Telemetry vendors:
- By default telemetry is metadata only (latency, status codes, trace ids, sample error messages). We do NOT send full request or response bodies to third-party telemetry vendors in the hosted configuration.
- For customers who enable advanced request-level debugging, we provide an opt-in debug mode that can capture payloads; this mode is disabled by default and controlled via an admin setting.
- Action: We can include a clause in the DPA that telemetry vendors will not receive request/response bodies unless explicitly enabled by the customer.

2) Cloud providers / log locality:
- Hosted: logs for the hosted offering are stored in the region of the tenant (US or EU). Our US region stores logs in AWS us-west-2 by default.
- Dedicated/Private: we support customer-managed storage and VPC-only access for strict residency.
- Action: We can commit to keeping Acme's hosted logs in US-only buckets; will include in the MSA/DPA language and provide an additional technical note for your infra team.

3) Marketplace (Azure):
- Marketplace procurement triggers billing metadata to Microsoft (invoice amounts, subscription identifiers). Microsoft does not receive request payloads as part of marketplace billing flows.
- If you require marketplace procurement but want additional controls, we can discuss a private offer where billing flows are mediated differently.

4) Automatic PII redaction:
- Redwood provides a set of built-in redaction rules for common patterns (emails, SSNs, credit card numbers) as a configurable option. Redaction runs at ingestion before storage of logs when enabled.
- For AI-specific sensitive items in model outputs, we recommend a two-pronged approach: prompt engineering to avoid eliciting PII and post-response filters that redact patterns or replace tokens with placeholders.

Next steps / asks:
- Logan: can you confirm exact telemetry vendor list and add the opt-in debug mode details to the subprocessor appendix?
- Dev: please review DPA clause language (I attached the DPA draft) and flag any terms that require legal redlines for enterprise customers.
- Alice/Bob: let us know if Acme needs the SOC2 report to be attested to a specific auditor name (attached) or a custom audit addendum.

I can put together a short technical note for your infra/security team that spells out where logs live and how the redaction flow works — would you like that before we finalize the DPA?

Best,
Marissa

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Forwarding Acme thread — summary of asks and owners:

1) Telemetry: confirm that hosted telemetry does NOT include request/response bodies by default and produce one-paragraph language we can add to the DPA. (Owner: Logan)
2) Subprocessor appendix: include Sentry/Datadog entries + note about opt-in debug mode and how customers can enable/disable. Also add cloud infra (AWS/GCP) and Azure marketplace note. (Owner: Logan)
3) Legal redlines: review attached DPA and flag any non-standard items for enterprise deals (data retention commitments, redaction SLA, subprocessor notification cadence). (Owner: Dev)
4) Tech note: produce a short log-locality + redaction flow doc we can share with Acme security. If possible include architecture diagram (simple) and retention options. (Owner: Logan)

Timeline: Acme asked for answers this week to avoid procurement delays. Can we get first drafts by Thu 26 Mar EOD? If anyone needs extension, flag now so I can push expectations with the buyer.

Thanks — I will attach the SOC2 and subprocessor list to the HubSpot deal and update the MAP once we have the DPA language.
